properties.name: Fur sales ban: Israel
properties.placed at: (the middle of the country (a country-wide record))
properties.what: Israel's environmental protection minister Gila Gamliel signed regulations in 2021 banning the sale of fur for fashion, in force six months after signing, the first national fur sales ban; exemptions cover scientific research, education and religious purposes or tradition (e.g. shtreimel hats).

properties.name: Fur farming status: India
properties.placed at: (the middle of the country (a country-wide record))
properties.what: India banned imports of mink, fox and chinchilla skins in January 2017.

properties.name: Denmark's 2020 COVID-19 mink cull
properties.placed at: (the middle of the country (a country-wide record))
properties.what: After COVID-19 was found on mink farms, the Danish government announced on 4 November 2020 that all mink in Denmark would be culled; parliament passed legal authority only on 21 December 2020, and the Mink Commission reported on 30 June 2022 that the order lacked legal authority. Mink breeding was banned until 31 December 2022. Before the cull Denmark produced about 40% of the world's mink pelts. Figures: About 17 million mink on Danish farms before the cull; 15.5 million culled 10 Oct–30 Nov 2020 across 1,182 herds; almost 800 farms in 2019; 24.5 million pelts exported in 2019 worth DKK 4.9 billion; compensation estimate just under DKK 24 billion (Jan 2024)

properties.name: British Columbia mink farming phase-out
properties.placed at: British Columbia, British Columbia (the middle of the state or region named)
properties.what: British Columbia introduced a phase-out of mink farming in 2021, to be completed by April 2023, after coronavirus outbreaks on its mink farms.

properties.name: São Paulo state fur farming ban
properties.what: São Paulo state banned fur farming in 2014 and fur imports in 2015, per HSI's 2015 list.

properties.name: California fur sales ban
properties.placed at: California, California (the middle of the state or region named)
properties.what: California's Assembly Bill 44, authored by Laura Friedman and passed in 2019, banned the sale and manufacture of new fur from 2023, the first US state to do so; vintage fur is exempt and stores selling fur face penalties of $500 to $1,000. It followed city bans in West Hollywood, Berkeley, San Francisco and Los Angeles. Figures: Penalties $500–$1,000; 12 US cities had passed laws phasing out new fur sales, five in Massachusetts (Jan 2023)

properties.name: Saga Furs
properties.what: Finnish fur auction company founded in 1938 by the Finnish Fur Breeders, headquartered in Vantaa; it deals only in farmed fur, mainly mink, fox and finnraccoon, and holds its sales in Helsinki. After the wind-down of Kopenhagen Fur it is described as the world's largest fur auction house; North American mink is graded at its facility in Milton, Wisconsin, and it took over North American Fur Auctions' ranched mink loan portfolio in 2019.

properties.name: Saga Furs North America facility
properties.what: US subsidiary of Saga Furs where North American mink pelts are processed and graded before being sold at auction in Helsinki.

properties.name: Kopenhagen Fur
properties.what: Danish fur auction house at Langagervej 60, Glostrup, which mainly sold the output of the Danish Fur Breeders' Association; once the world's largest fur auction house. It announced in November 2020, after the Danish mink cull, that it would close within three years, and held its final auction in summer 2024; the headquarters was offered for sale at DKK 630 million in November 2024. Figures: About 500 buyers from 15 countries bid on some 12 million mink pelts (1999); could sort 150,000 furs a day at peak; reported 40% of global mink fur production (2020). HSUS gives founding year 1930; the property listing says the final auction ended 78 years of operation.

properties.name: North American Fur Auctions (NAFA)
properties.what: Toronto-based fur auction house, successor to the Hudson's Bay Company fur auction business (HBC founded 1670), owned by the trappers and farmers who shipped to it and the largest of the three North American fur auction houses. It acquired American Legend Cooperative and the Blackglama brand in April 2018, was granted creditor protection in October 2019 after a lender withdrew, and closed; its ranched mink loan portfolio was sold to Saga Furs.

properties.name: Fur Harvesters Auction
properties.what: Trapper-owned fur auction house in North Bay, Ontario, opened in 1959 by the Ontario Trappers Association and reopened by the fur harvesters group in 1991 after the association went into receivership. It sells most farmed fox pelts from Canada and the US and is now the only auction house selling North American wild fur; it is the exclusive auction for Northwest Territories and Nunavut fur brands. Figures: Four auctions a year bringing in about $10–11 million annually

properties.name: American Legend Cooperative
properties.what: Seattle-headquartered cooperative of US mink farmers, formed in 1986 by merging the Great Lakes Mink Association (1941) and the Mutation Mink Breeders Association (1942), and owner of the Blackglama brand. It announced it was winding down in 2018; North American Fur Auctions acquired it and Blackglama in April 2018. Figures: Membership required selling over 1,200 mink pelts at its auctions in the previous year

properties.name: Sojuzpushnina fur auctions
properties.what: State-owned Soyuzpushnina has held fur auctions in Saint Petersburg (Leningrad) three to four times a year since 1931, specialising in sable, whose prices set the world price; auctions are held at the House of Furs, 98 Moskovsky Avenue (built 1937–39). It became a joint stock company in 1998 with the state as sole shareholder. Figures: Sales about $128 million (1989) and about $8 million (1999)

properties.name: Shangcun fur market
properties.placed at: Shangcun, Hebei (the middle of the state or region named)
properties.what: Fur market in Shangcun, Suning (Shuning) county, Hebei, about 100 km south of Beijing, described as China's largest fur goods trading region and the rural centre of China's raw pelt trade; on set days of the lunar month it becomes an open-air market where animals are also killed and skinned on site (Toronto Star, 2012). It hosted the sixth China Fur Fair in 2005. Figures: More than 60% of China's unprocessed fur trade (2012); 350+ fur goods factories, production about 2.8 billion yuan and exports about $117 million (23% of national fur exports) in 2004; Suning county: about 180 million pieces of leather traded a year, ~70% of national volume, 1,730+ fur clothing firms (2020)

properties.name: Chongfu fur market
properties.placed at: Chongfu, Zhejiang (the middle of the state or region named)
properties.what: Chongfu fur clothing market in Tongxiang, Zhejiang; in 2006 it was described as China's largest fur trading area. Figures: Production value over 4.5 billion yuan (about $567 million) in 2005; about 60% of Zhejiang's and 40% of China's fur business (China Leather Industry Association)

properties.name: Haining China Leather City
properties.what: Leather and fur market complex in Haining, about 125 km west of Shanghai, described by the South China Morning Post as China's fur hub. Figures: Complex covers 350 hectares; Haining makes about half of all fur and leather products made in China

properties.name: Fur sales ban: Los Angeles
properties.what: The Los Angeles City Council tentatively voted 13–1 on 12 February 2019 to ban the sale and manufacture of new fur products, with the ban starting 1 January 2021. Figures: Vote 13–1; effective 1 January 2021

properties.name: Fur sales ban: San Francisco
properties.what: San Francisco's Board of Supervisors voted in March 2018 to ban the sale of new fur products; the ban took effect 1 January 2019, with existing inventory sellable until 1 January 2020.

properties.name: Fur sales ban: Berkeley
properties.what: Berkeley passed a ban on sales of new fur products in 2017.

properties.name: Fur sales ban: West Hollywood
properties.what: West Hollywood passed a ban on sales of new fur apparel in 2013.

properties.name: COVID-19 mink cull: Netherlands
properties.what: SARS-CoV-2 was found on Dutch mink farms from spring 2020, after mandatory screening began on 25 May; infected farms were culled from 5 June 2020, starting with a farm in Deurne, and ten farms in North Brabant and Limburg were ordered culled in early June. The government brought the end of mink farming forward first to 1 March 2021 and then to 1 January 2021. Figures: Mink at 69 farms tested positive and 68 farms culled (Wageningen University, 25 Oct 2020); first culled farm at Deurne had about 1,500 mother mink, each with 4–5 pups; about 130 farms remaining (Aug 2020); 25 infected farms by 17 July 2020

properties.name: COVID-19 mink cull: Puebla de Valverde
properties.placed at: La Puebla de Valverde, Aragón (the middle of the state or region named)
properties.what: Aragón's regional authorities ordered on 13 July 2020 the culling of all 92,700 mink on a farm in Puebla de Valverde (Teruel) after tests found 87% of the animals infected with SARS-CoV-2; the outbreak was traced after a farm employee's wife fell ill in May and seven farm workers tested positive. Figures: 92,700 mink culled; 87% of animals tested positive; Spain had 38 mink farms (31 in Galicia)

properties.name: COVID-19 mink cull: Kozani and Siatista
properties.what: Greek authorities announced on 13 November 2020 the culling of mink on infected farms in Kozani prefecture, including one near Siatista; tests in Kastoria found 10 infections among farm workers. No number of culled mink was given. Figures: At least 2 infected farms; 10 infected workers in Kastoria

properties.name: Siatista fur trade
properties.what: Siatista's economy is based on the fur trade, with furriers working mink, fox, sable and chinchilla for domestic and international markets (Wikipedia, claim marked 'citation needed').

properties.name: Kastoria fur trade and International Fur Fair
properties.what: Kastoria has worked fur since the early Middle Ages, when it supplied ermine for Byzantine courtiers; the industry was established in the 16th century and in the 17th century the town was Europe's fur marketplace, importing Russian sable. Mink now predominates. The Kastoria International Fur Fair, first held in 1976, held its 51st edition on 16–19 April 2026 with participants from more than 45 countries. Figures: More than 45 countries at the 51st fair (2026); about 80 mink farms in the Kastoria area (Euronews, 2021); about 25,000 Kastorian furriers in New York in the 1980s; 300+ fur dealers in the town (Wikipedia, 'citation needed')

properties.name: Hong Kong International Fur & Fashion Fair
properties.placed at: Wan Chai, Hong Kong (the middle of the country)
properties.what: Annual fur trade fair at the Hong Kong Convention and Exhibition Centre; the 2025 edition ran 19–22 February with 56 exhibitors, and PETA Asia protested outside. The Hong Kong Fur Federation's director said the fair accounts for up to 70% of the industry's yearly consumption (his claim). Figures: 56 exhibitors (12 from mainland China) in 2025; Hong Kong was the world's sixth-largest fur export hub in 2021

properties.name: Brühl fur trade centre, Leipzig
properties.what: The Brühl street in Leipzig was the international centre of the fur trade until the 1930s; in the 1920s it represented one-third of world fur trade. In 1938 the Nazi government took the Jewish-owned fur firms from their owners. After the Second World War Frankfurt replaced Leipzig as Germany's fur centre. Figures: One-third of world fur trade (1920s); 8.7% of Jewish Leipzigers worked in the fur industry vs 4.2% of all Leipzigers

properties.name: Hudson's Bay Company fur sales, Beaver House, London
properties.what: Beaver House on Garlick Hill in the City of London was the Hudson's Bay Company's headquarters until 1970 and housed one of the world's largest fur auction houses, the base of London's fur trade; a 1974 photograph shows HBC staff sizing graded mink there. HBC later sold its Canadian fur-auction business to Hudson's Bay Fur Sales Canada, which became North American Fur Auctions. Figures: HBC founded 1670

properties.what: USDA's annual mink survey reports Wisconsin mink pelt production and the number of female mink bred to produce kits. Wisconsin is the largest US mink-producing state. Figures: pelts produced: 514,130 (2023), 438,710 (2024); females bred to produce kits: 118,290 (2024), 105,850 (2025); US total pelts 957,410 (2023), 771,200 (2024)

properties.name: Mink farms, Kastoria
properties.what: Greek mink farming is concentrated in Kastoria and Siatista in northern Greece. After sanctions on Russia, the main buyer, 40 of 92 mink farms had shut down by early 2023. Figures: 92 mink farms, 40 shut down; remaining farms expected to raise one million mink, down from 1.8 million in past years (2023)

properties.name: Fox, raccoon dog and mink farms, Hebei
properties.placed at: Hebei, Hebei (the middle of the state or region named)
properties.what: Humane Society International investigators visited five fur farms in Hebei and Liaoning in December 2023, each holding about 2,000–4,000 fur-bearing animals in cages. Investigators from Swiss Animal Protection and EAST International also visited fur farms in Hebei in 2004–2005, holding 50 to 6,000 animals each. Figures: 2,000–4,000 animals per farm (2023); China produced 10 million fox, mink and raccoon dog pelts in 2023, about 22 million in 2022, 87 million in 2014 (60m mink, 14m raccoon dog, 13m fox)

properties.name: Mink farms, Greater Poland Voivodeship
properties.placed at: Greater Poland Voivodeship, Greater Poland Voivodeship (the middle of the state or region named)
properties.what: Polish fur production, mainly American mink, is concentrated in two provinces, West Pomeranian and Greater Poland, according to a 2018 study for the Fur Free Alliance. Figures: 700–750 carnivore fur farms in Poland; 8.5 million pelts claimed for 2016 (2018 study); 476 active farms in the Chief Veterinary Inspectorate registry (2020)

properties.name: Mink farm complex, Góreczki
properties.placed at: Góreczki, Greater Poland Voivodeship (the middle of the state or region named)
properties.what: Mink farm in Góreczki, Koźmin Wielkopolski commune, owned by Wojciech Wójcik according to Anima International, which described it in 2020 as probably the biggest mink farm in the world. A 2018 study counted a cluster of about 51 registered companies at Góreczki. The Wójcik family owns 56 of Poland's 476 registered farms, per the veterinary registry. Figures: about half a million mink (investigator's contact, 2020); ~51 registered companies at the site (2018)

properties.name: Mink farms, Nowogard commune
properties.what: A 2018 study lists one farm above 210 livestock units (about 84,000 mink) in Nowogard commune and 7 registered fur facilities in the commune. Figures: 7 facilities registered; 1 above 210 LU (1 LU = 400 mink)

properties.name: Mink farms, Czerniejewo commune
properties.what: A 2018 study lists two fur farms above 210 livestock units (about 84,000 mink each) in Czerniejewo commune. Figures: 2 farms above 210 LU (1 LU = 400 mink)

properties.name: Fox and mink farms, Ostrobothnia
properties.placed at: Ostrobothnia, Ostrobothnia, South Ostrobothnia, Central Ostrobothnia, North Ostrobothnia (the middle of the country)
properties.what: The large majority of Finland's fur farms are in the south, central and north regions of Ostrobothnia (Yle, 2023). Finland is described by its industry as the world's largest producer of certified fox pelts. Figures: 442 FIFUR member farms nationally (Dec 2023)
